summary: An 1858 Egyptian Revival iron tower on Atchafalaya Bay, discontinued in 1916 and moved ashore to a Berwick, Louisiana, park in 1987-1990.

lens.where: Original cupola and lens missing (NRHP); a Fresnel lens of unknown origin is at Berwick Town Hall (Friends)

structures.note: Egyptian Revival; on iron screw-pile platform until 1987; moved to Berwick park 1990 or 1991

access.note: Everett S. Berry Memorial Lighthouse Park, Berwick; grounds open daily; tower closed to visitors (Friends)

events.note: Red light first shown 1 September 1859 (Friends; Cajun Coast)
Confederates deactivate the light in its third year; dark through the Civil War (Friends)
Lamps and lens recovered from St. Martinville; reactivated summer 1865 (Friends). A Board notice (Tribune, 5 Nov 1865) gives a fixed red light shown on the night of the 8th of October
October 1867 hurricane damages the exposed tower and dwelling (Friends)
Red light replaced by a white light from 1 February 1868, per a Notice to Mariners (New Orleans Republican, 18 January 1868)
Congress appropriates $5,000 to elevate the tower and $15,000 for a steam fog signal (Friends)
Tower detached, bolted to four cast-iron columns and lowered back, nearly doubling the buffer between the lighthouse and the bay (Friends)
Twelve-inch steam whistle begins operation 31 March 1875 (Friends)
Steam whistle replaced by a 1,200-pound fog bell (Friends)
16-17 August 1915 hurricane destroys the platform under the dwelling and outbuildings (Lighthouse Service Bulletin)
Discontinued when the Point Au Fer Reef light was activated, 31 March 1916 (Friends; Commissioner report FY1916)
House Bill 1080 transfers ownership from the state to Berwick (Friends)
Removed from its pilings on 8 October 1987 (Friends)
Moved to the present park site; April 1990 (Friends; Cajun Coast); the nomination says April 1991
Louisiana state historic preservation officer certifies the National Register nomination, 29 July 1991
Doors and windows installed and a replica lantern room placed on top (Friends)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record says 1848; the nomination and Cajun Coast say the tower was built in 1858, and Friends says Congress appropriated money for it in 1856. No source supports 1848 for the tower.

Friends dates the reactivation to summer 1865, on the sixth anniversary of first lighting. A Lighthouse Board notice in the New Orleans Tribune (5 November 1865) says the repaired light showed a fixed red light on the night of the 8th of the month (the notice is dated 18 October). The notice is the nearer primary source; the story gives both.
The move to the park: April 1990 (Friends; Cajun Coast) against April 1991 (nomination). Both are recorded in the story.

corrections.why: First shown 1 September 1859 (Friends; Cajun Coast; USLHS also gives 1859 first lit). The record gives 1858.
NRHP and Cajun Coast date the tower to 1858; no source supports 1848.

notes_for_editor: Thin on primary records: the Board reports before 1891 are not in the corpus, so the 1856 appropriation, 1859 first light, 1865 relighting, 1867 hurricane, 1873 appropriation and 1889 fog bell rest on LighthouseFriends alone. The Commissioner FY1916 table lists 'Southwest Reef, La' among discontinued entries with an '8-inch air whistle' (scan p. 152); the columns are OCR-split and read by position; not used in the story. Record characteristic 'Fl W 6s' is not supported by these sources (the light showed red when new; a 1868 notice says it became white from 1 February 1868; the 6-second flash is not in the sources); not changed. Record lat/lon sits about 0.7 km from the USLHS coordinates (29 41.39 N, 91 12.58 W) at the park; not changed. The record's related replica (us-az-berwick) was not checked. The USCG Historian's Southwest Reef page is blocked (403 on the archived copy); the Atchafalaya Heritage blog redirect loops; their search snippets are not cited. A Louisiana newspaper search (Chronicling America, 1859 to 1916) was started but did not complete within this run; no newspaper text is cited. The nomination's certification date (29 July 1991) is used as the event; the record's 1991 'nrhp_listed' is not separately sourced. Roster: the archive lists no names between 1861 and 1865; 'Edward Rollingson' (1881-83) and 'Edward L. Rollingson' appear as separate archive records with separate person slugs; kept as the archive prints them. Cajun Coast's 'open daily' refers to the park; Friends says the tower is closed. New Orleans Tribune 5 Nov 1865 p.4 Notice to Mariners: OCR date line reads 'Oct. 18, 1866'; the paper is 1865, so the notice is read as October 1865; the page image should be checked. Notice gives range 12 nautical miles (not in the record). The same paper and 1865 search also carry repeated copies of the notice (pp. 4 of 24 Oct to 12 Nov). Friends says the 1856 appropriation was for a lighthouse to replace the lightship and the Point Au Fer light; the Point Au Fer light's keeper record is only in Friends. Story pass 2026-10-22 (resume): the record's 1875 event note said the lowering nearly doubled the tower's height above water; Friends says the buffer between the lighthouse and the bay was nearly doubled, and the event note now says so. The Tribune notice dated "Oct. 18" carries the OCR year 1866 on a paper printed in 1865; the story gives the date without a year. Friends puts the reactivation in summer 1865 on the sixth anniversary of the first lighting; the notice shows the light in October, and the story says so. Edward Rollingson (1881-83) and Edward L. Rollingson (1894-98) are separate roster records; the story does not link the 1880s stint to the later head keeper.
